hook: How an app switches off Apple Intelligence and keeps its models gone.
the_question: RemoveMacAI, per its README, turns off Apple Intelligence and deletes its models. How does macOS stay off instead of downloading them again?
the_intuition: The obvious guess is a single hidden switch that the app flips. The README describes three separate mechanisms instead.
mechanism: Locked settings, including the AI ones, go into a configuration profile. The user approves it in System Settings. Removing the profile reverts them.
Models are removed through Apple's asset service. The profile also redirects their downloads to a closed local port, so macOS does not re-fetch them.
Other settings are written the way defaults write does. Old values go into a journal file, so undo restores them exactly.
why_it_matters: The README says every change is reviewed before it is applied and can be undone, and that System Integrity Protection stays on.
the_catch: An announcement by the maker, not a study. The README says it cannot delete Apple's built-in apps, and macOS updates may reset some settings.
caption: RemoveMacAI does not just flip a switch. Per its README, a profile locks Apple Intelligence off, the models are deleted, and their downloads are sent to a closed port. Other tweaks are journaled so undo works. Would you keep Apple Intelligence on or switch it off?
alt_text: An eight-slide carousel explaining how the open-source RemoveMacAI app turns off Apple Intelligence on macOS 27: a configuration profile locks the settings, the models are removed and their downloads redirected to a closed local port, and other settings are journaled so undo restores them. Based on the maker's README.

es.hook: Cómo una app desactiva Apple Intelligence y mantiene sus modelos eliminados
es.the_question: RemoveMacAI, según su README, apaga Apple Intelligence y borra sus modelos. ¿Cómo logra macOS permanecer sin ellos en lugar de volver a descargarlos?
es.the_intuition: La suposición obvia es que existe un interruptor oculto que la app activa. Sin embargo, el README describe tres mecanismos distintos.
mechanism: Los ajustes bloqueados, incluidos los de IA, se guardan en un perfil de configuración. El usuario lo aprueba en Configuración del Sistema. Al eliminar el perfil, los ajustes vuelven a su estado original.
Los modelos se eliminan mediante el servicio de activos de Apple. El perfil también redirige sus descargas a un puerto local cerrado, de modo que macOS no los vuelve a obtener.
Otros ajustes se escriben como lo hace defaults. Los valores antiguos se guardan en un archivo de registro, por lo que deshacer los cambios los restaura exactamente.
es.why_it_matters: El README indica que cada cambio se revisa antes de aplicarse y puede revertirse, y que la Protección de Integridad del Sistema permanece activada.
es.the_catch: Es un anuncio del creador, no un estudio. El README aclara que no puede eliminar las aplicaciones integradas de Apple, y que actualizaciones de macOS podrían restablecer algunos ajustes.
